title: Arbitrary Ancilla Manipulation in Quantum Encryption
summary: Correctness is specified for honest encryption with a zero-initialized ancilla; characterizing the transformation under arbitrary ancilla manipulation remains open.

formal_statement.body: For an encryption map $\operatorname{Enc}_k$ implemented by a quantum transformation $\sum_{x,y}\alpha_{x,y}\lvert x,y\rangle\mapsto\sum_{x,y}\alpha_{x,y}\lvert\phi_{x,y}\rangle$, the ancilla register $y$ has length $\lvert\operatorname{Enc}_k(x)\rvert-\lvert x\rvert$, and correctness is required when $y=0$ through $\phi_{x,0}=\operatorname{Enc}_k(x)$. Determine and characterize the transformation's behavior when the ancilla is not initialized to $\lvert0\rangle$ and can instead be manipulated arbitrarily, while retaining the stated correctness condition for honest, zero-initialized execution.

scope.domain: Quantum encryption implementations with ancilla registers subject to arbitrary manipulation.
assumptions: Honest execution initializes the ancilla to the zero state and satisfies the stated encryption correctness condition.
parameters: k: the key selecting the encryption map
y: the ancilla register, whose prescribed length is the encryption-output length minus the input length
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine and characterize the transformation's behavior when the ancilla is not initialized to the zero state and may be manipulated arbitrarily, while retaining honest-execution correctness.

citations.label: Semantic Security and Indistinguishability in the Quantum World

progress.summary: The source specifies correct behavior for a zero-initialized ancilla in honest execution. It explicitly leaves arbitrary ancilla manipulation as an interesting open problem.
citation_labels: Tommaso Gagliardoni et al., Semantic Security and Indistinguishability in the Quantum World
